lbl_adv_general: Advanced Settings (Do not change unless certain)
hint_logging_level:
Select the detail level printed to the live console:
• DEBUG: Everything (Extremely verbose)
• INFO: Normal updates and progress
• WARNING: Minor issues that do not halt the program
• ERROR: Failed tasks or skipped files
• CRITICAL: Application crashes

Deviation: Third-party libraries (Pillow, AV, urllib3) are capped at INFO level even in DEBUG mode to prevent binary dumps.
hint_no_retry:
By default, only files that successfully processed ('OK') are skipped on subsequent runs.
Select other statuses here if you want to skip them as well.
lbl_img_range:
Target Image Range
(Ignore this setting if each of your files contains a single image)
hint_img_range:
For files that hold several images (e.g., TIFF), specify which ones to extract.
Examples:
• Images 2 to 8: '2-8'
• First 10 images: '-10'
• Image 10 onwards to the end of the file: '10-'
• Images 3, 6, and 10 to 15: '3, 6, 10-15'
• Leave empty to process ALL frames contained in a multi-image file.
lbl_size_pipeline: How the file size is controlled:
hint_size_pipeline:
1. The image is shrunk so its longest side fits {resolution} (small images are never enlarged).
2. Quality is lowered step by step from maximum to minimum until the file fits under the {size}.
3. Quality never drops below {quality} — if the file still does not fit, it is saved larger than the target, and the report says so.
Files still too large? Lower {resolution} — it is by far the strongest lever.
hint_jpeg_quality:
Determines how sharp the image should look. Bounds: 1 to 100.
• 90 = High Quality (Recommended)
• 75 = Good Quality (Web Standard)
• 50 = Medium Quality
• 20 = Lowest acceptable (below this, our tests showed visible discoloration)
• 10 = Terrible Quality (Heavy compression)
hint_max_size:
A soft target, not a hard limit.
The app reduces image quality until the file fits under this size.
If even the {quality} is not small enough, the file is saved anyway — larger than this target — and the report notes it.
To make files reliably smaller, lower {resolution} instead.
Must be >= 1.
hint_lowest_qual:
The quality level the app refuses to go below, even if the file then exceeds the {size}.
Without this floor, the app would keep degrading an image just to hit a size number.
In our testing, a floor of 10 produced visibly discolored photos, while 20 still looked good — hence the default of 20.
Bounds: 1 to 100.
hint_max_dim:
The strongest file-size lever. Images larger than this are shrunk proportionally (both sides equally, no distortion) until their longest side equals this value; smaller images are never enlarged.
Halving this value roughly quarters the file size.
Must be >= 1.
Reference values:
• 3840 (4K) = maximum detail
• 2560 (QHD) = balanced
• 1920 (Full HD) = default, compact files
hint_white_bg: Provide an RGB tuple (e.g., 255,255,255) used to fill in transparent areas when flattening PNG images into JPEG format.
hint_pillow_max:
Upper limit on the pixel count of a single image; protects memory when reading very large or very dense images.
Must be >= 1.
lbl_name_prefix_len: Original name in output file names (characters):
hint_name_prefix_len:
How many characters of the original file name to keep in each output file name, after the file number. 0 = numbers only, e.g. '1_page_3.jpg'.
Bounds: 0 to 64.
lbl_name_timestamps: Capture time in video frame names:
hint_name_timestamps: Appends each video frame's capture time ('_tHH_MM_SS_ff') to its file name.
hint_doc_range:
Define exactly which PDF pages to extract. Examples:
• Pages 2 to 8: '2-8'
• First 10 pages: '-10'
• Page 10 onwards to the end of the file: '10-'
• Leave empty to extract ALL pages.
lbl_doc_max: Maximum number of pages per file:
hint_doc_max:
No more than this many pages are extracted from a single document; extra pages are skipped and the report notes it. Also protects your computer from huge PDF books.
Must be >= 1.
hint_pdf_scale:
Controls the rendering resolution of PDF text.
For clearer images, increase sharpness and {resolution}.
Reference values:
• High: Text Sharpness 4 + {resolution} 3840
• Standard: Text Sharpness 2 + {resolution} 1920 (default)
• Low: Text Sharpness 1 + {resolution} 1920
Must be >= 1.
hint_anim_range:
Define exactly which GIF/WebP frames to extract. Examples:
• Frames 2 to 8: '2-8'
• First 10 frames: '-10'
• Frames 10 onwards to the end of the file: '10-'
• Leave empty to process ALL items contained in a file.

ORDER OF OPERATIONS:
1. The program first filters the animation to ONLY the frames you specify here.
2. It then applies the numerical limit below to that filtered pool by down-sampling it.
hint_anim_target:
How many frames to extract from the pool selected above.
Must be >= 1.
hint_scene_sens:
Compares pixels to skip consecutive frames that look visually identical.
• 0.0 = Keep all frames (No filtering)
• 2.0 = Strict (Minor noise allowed)
• 5.0 = Moderate (Skips talking heads)
• 15.0 = Loose (Aggressively skips most static scenes)
Must be >= 0.0.
hint_vid_mode:
• SUMMARY: Extracts a fixed number of frames across the whole video (e.g., exactly 10 frames).
• SAMPLING: Extracts frames at a fixed time interval (e.g., 1 frame every 5 seconds).
hint_vid_range:
Format MUST be strict HH:MM:SS.
Examples:
• First 10 seconds: '00:00:00-00:00:10'
• One minute to two minutes: '00:01:00-00:02:00'
• Specific times: '00:00:15, 00:00:30, 00:00:45-00:01:00'
• Leave empty to process the whole video.
hint_vid_sum_frames:
Total frames extracted uniformly across the video if Mode is SUMMARY.
Must be >= 1.
hint_vid_samp_fps: How many pictures to capture every second if Mode is SAMPLING. Must be > 0.0.
hint_vid_samp_max:
Hard cap on frames per video in SAMPLING mode.
If the rate would produce more, only the first N frames are kept and the rest of the video is skipped; the report notes it.
Must be >= 1.
hint_llm_provider: Select the API dialect and ecosystem you wish to use.
hint_llm_max_jpegs:
How many images are sent to the AI per HTTP request.
For each file it makes a separate request to the AI
If we can fit all of the images from this file into a single AI request then there will be only one request per file
If there are more images from a single file than this setting then it will make multiple AI requests
Example: If set to 10 and a video has 30 frames, it will make 3 separate AI requests.
Increase this number if the AI must receive all pages/frames/images together for context.
Each request is separate: the AI cannot compare images across requests. Images are numbered and labelled with their page and, for videos, their time, so answers may refer to them by number.
Providers cap the size of one request; if a file fails with a 'too large' reply, lower this number or the {size} in the Output tab.
hint_llm_parse_err:
If the server's reply itself cannot be read: garbled text, an unexpected reply layout, or an answer cut off by the token limit. Not about the AI's answer inside it.
Checked: halt the entire batch. Unchecked: log the error and move on to the next file.
hint_llm_abort_malformed:
Under the hood the AI sends its answer in a machine format, JSON, which the app turns into rows of the results table. If the answer is still not valid after all attempts, the app cannot turn it into rows.
Checked: halt the entire batch. Unchecked: keep the raw answer, mark the file's AI result as invalid, and move on to the next file.
hint_llm_max_fails:
The app halts when this many files in a row fail with no successful reply in between. Two separate counts share this limit: files where the AI server failed, and files where the AI's answer could not be turned into table rows.
Must be >= 1.
hint_llm_retries:
Total tries per request, including the first. 1 = never retry.
Only transient failures are retried (rate limits, server errors, connection problems); a request the provider rejects outright is recorded at once and not re-sent.
lbl_llm_json_attempts: Attempts to get a readable answer:
hint_llm_json_attempts:
Total tries per request, including the first. 1 = never retry. Each retry sends the images again, so it costs time and, with a paid provider, money.
Must be >= 1.
hint_llm_output_mode:
• One answer per file: the AI answers once for the whole file. One row per file in the results.
• One answer per image: the AI answers separately for every page or frame. One row per image, each with its page number and, for videos, its time.
A file with more images than {images} is sent in several requests. In per-file mode each request gets its own row.
hint_llm_output_columns:
Write the columns you want the AI to fill in. Separate names with a comma or put one per line.
Example: 'vendor, total, date' tells the AI to fill in three columns. In the results spreadsheet they appear as 'llm_vendor', 'llm_total' and 'llm_date'.
The default, 'answer', gives one column, 'llm_answer', holding the AI's whole reply.
The name 'page' is reserved: the app fills that one in itself. Cannot be empty.
hint_llm_column_meanings:
Optional. Explain in plain words what each column should contain. Sent to the AI word for word after your prompt.
Example: 'vendor: the shop name as printed; total: the amount paid, digits only; date: as DD.MM.YYYY'.
hint_llm_timeout:
Max wait time in seconds for the AI network response.
Must be >= 1.
hint_llm_sleep:
Pause duration in seconds between consecutive network retries.
Must be >= 0.
hint_prov_url: The official API endpoint address for {provider}. For local providers (like LM Studio or Ollama), this is usually a localhost address (e.g., http://localhost:1234/v1/chat/completions).
hint_prov_model: The exact identifier for the {provider} model you wish to use (e.g., 'gpt-5.6' or 'claude-sonnet-5'). Ensure this matches the provider's official model list perfectly to avoid routing errors.
hint_local_context: Local servers start with a small context window (Ollama and LM Studio: 4096 tokens), and one image costs about 2,500 tokens. Raise the context length in the server itself (Ollama: OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH; LM Studio: the model's load settings) or set {images} to 1. These details change between versions: search online for the current way to set it.
hint_prov_token: Enter a token and apply the change to save it on this computer.
hint_auth_key: Defines the HTTP header name used to authenticate with the AI provider. Standard APIs typically use 'Authorization' (OpenAI) or 'x-api-key' (Anthropic). Check your provider's API documentation if you are unsure.
hint_auth_fmt: Specifies the exact format of the authentication string. The application will automatically swap '{token}' with your actual API key. For example, OpenAI requires 'Bearer {token}', while Anthropic just needs '{token}' by itself.
hint_extra_key: An optional secondary HTTP header required by certain API ecosystems. For instance, Anthropic Claude strictly requires an 'anthropic-version' header to process requests. Leave this blank if your provider does not require one.
hint_extra_val: The exact value to pass alongside the {setting} above. For example, if using Anthropic, this is usually set to a date like '2023-06-01'. Leave blank if unused.
hint_req_max: Check this box to send the reply-length ceiling below with every request. OpenAI treats it as optional; Anthropic Claude rejects a request without it.
hint_max_tokens_field: The request field that carries the ceiling. OpenAI's gpt-5 family rejects 'max_tokens' and wants 'max_completion_tokens'; the other presets use 'max_tokens'. Sent only when {setting} is ticked.
err_max_tokens_field_invalid: Enter the field name without spaces, e.g. 'max_tokens'.
hint_max_val:
Active only when {setting} is enabled.
The ceiling on the reply length in tokens (pieces of words), the model's thinking included. Too low cuts the answer off and the run halts with a token-limit error; raise it if that happens.
hint_sys_loc:
OpenAI expects the system prompt as the first entry in the 'messages' array.
Anthropic Claude requires it explicitly separated at the 'top_level' of the payload.
hint_img_payload:
'data_uri': Standard web formatting (data:image/jpeg;base64,...).
'base64_dict': Raw data inside a nested source dictionary (used by Claude).
hint_extract_path:
The exact JSON bracket path to locate the AI's text response.
• OpenAI/Custom: 'choices[0].message.content'
• Anthropic Claude: 'content[0].text'
hint_reasoning:
Determines how AI reasoning is handled:
• preserve: Keeps all text intact.
• strip_xml: Removes <think> tags (Ollama/Local).
• parse_claude_blocks: Filters Anthropic 'thinking' arrays.
• ignore_api_field: Ignores DeepSeek's dedicated reasoning fields.

err_archive_locked:
Could not archive the previous run's output folder because another program is still using files inside it.

Three ways to fix this:
1. Close any File Explorer windows, Excel, or image previews showing files from the output folder, then press "Start processing" again.
2. Rename or delete the "current_run" folder yourself, then press "Start processing" again. Renaming keeps the previous run's results; deleting throws them away.
3. Choose a different {output}, press "Apply Changes", then press "Start processing".
err_resume_old_database:
To start a new run:
1. Select {setting}.
2. Apply the change.
3. Start processing.

The previous results were created by an older version and cannot be resumed. Their folder will be archived.
err_resume_configuration_changed: The previous run's results database was recorded under different settings ({mode}, {format}, {columns}), so continuing it would mix two report shapes. Tick {setting}, apply the change and start again: the previous run's folder is archived and the new run starts clean.
err_resume_ai_work_changed: This run cannot continue because the source folder or processing settings changed. Select {setting}, apply the change, and start processing. The previous results will be archived.
err_run_start_unconfirmed: The application did not receive a reply to Start. Processing may have begun. If this message remains, close and reopen the application.
err_resume_ai_context_changed_detail: The source folder or effective processing settings changed.
err_settings_unreadable: The settings.json file could not be read.
err_settings_invalid: The saved settings have errors. Fix the highlighted fields, apply the changes and start again.
err_quality_floor_above_start: {floor} cannot be higher than {start}. The app starts compressing at {start} and, if an image is still too large, gradually lowers the quality — but never below {floor}. Setting the floor above the start is like setting a discount limit above the sticker price: the size limiter can never do its job. Please set {floor} equal to or below {start}.
